title: How advertising persuades

draft.title: How advertising persuades
card: Ads are made to make people want to buy. They often appeal to feelings, not just facts about the product.
Celebrity endorsement
a famous person is paid to use or praise a product, so fans link it with that person.
Limited-time offer
a deal that ends soon, such as 'today only', to make people feel they must buy now.
Bandwagon appeal
the ad says everyone is buying it, so you feel you should join in. An influencer post is similar to an endorsement: an online personality shows a product to their followers.
draft.remember: Ads use feelings and pressure, such as fame, deadlines and the crowd, to make you want to buy.

a.q: An ad says 'Join the millions of teens who already wear Zoomo shoes'. Which technique is this?
opts: A bandwagon appeal
A celebrity endorsement
A limited-time offer
An influencer post
a.why: The ad suggests that many people are buying, so you should join them. That is a bandwagon appeal. No famous person or deadline is named, so the other options do not fit.
a.clue: Who is the ad saying is buying the shoes?

b.q: A phone store posts 'Sale ends at midnight tonight, buy now!'. Which technique is it using, and how does it work?
opts: A limited-time offer, which makes people feel rushed
A bandwagon appeal, which says many people are buying
A celebrity endorsement, which links the phone to a star
An influencer post, which shows the phone to followers
b.why: The ad sets a deadline, so shoppers feel they must buy before it ends. That is a limited-time offer. It does not mention what others are buying, so it is not a bandwagon appeal.
b.clue: Look at what the ad says about time.

b.best: A limited-time offer, which makes people feel rushed

problems.detail: The influencer post definition sits inside the 'Bandwagon appeal' bullet. A student could read it as a kind of bandwagon appeal rather than a separate technique. It would be clearer as its own line.

proposal.title: How advertising persuades
card: Celebrity endorsement
a famous person, such as a sports star, is paid to use or praise a product. Fans may want it because they link it with that person.
Limited-time offer
a deal that ends soon, such as 'today only'. It makes people feel they must buy now, before they think it through.
Bandwagon appeal
the ad says lots of people already buy the product. You feel you should join in so you do not miss out.
Influencer post
an online personality shows or praises a product to their followers on social media. They may be paid or given free products, even if the post looks personal.
proposal.remember: Ads often play on feelings, not just facts: fame, deadlines, the crowd and online personalities can all make you want to buy.
